app.title: Note Trainer
app.tagline: Know the neck. Train the ear. Hold the time. The rest follows.

tip.fret: Fret tip: Memorise the reference dots on frets 3, 5 and 7.
tip.ear: Ear tip: Use headphones — bass and intonation are easier to hear.
tip.rhythm: Rhythm tip: Focus on the pulse before you play the note.

game.fret.tag: Find notes anywhere on the fretboard
game.fret.desc: You are given a note and a string. Find it and play it: the microphone listens and confirms. The whole neck, not only the first positions.

game.ear.tag: Name notes, chords and intervals by ear
game.ear.desc: One note, one answer. No microphone and no theory required: attention and a memory for sound.
game.rhythm.title: The Time
game.rhythm.tag: Groove, metronome and the sense of time
game.rhythm.desc: You play with the metronome and are judged to the millisecond. Subdivisions, syncopation, downbeat and upbeat — and one study without a metronome, to find out whether the time is truly yours.
hint.ear: No microphone here: you listen, then you answer.
hint.rhythm: Any note, any string. Only the moment you play it counts.
hint.uncalibrated: The input delay has not been measured: every note will read late. Twenty seconds settles it.
play.wrong_string: The note is right, the string is not: it lies on the {string}.
play.wrong_note: That was {played}. The note is {wanted}. Again.
play.drilling_weak: We work where you are weak. No clock: take the time you need and put them right, one by one.
ear.tier.easy_title: Three notes — the root, the major third and the fifth
ear.answer.interval_title: Name the distance from the home note — the skill that carries over to everything
ear.use_home_desc: Sounds the reference before every note. Take it away and you are left without support: quite another difficulty.
ear.intro: First the reference note, then the note to name. Answer with the buttons. Ten times, and then we shall see.
ear.intro_interval: First the reference note, then the note to name: tell me the INTERVAL between them. Intervals are the material melodies and chords are made of — this is where the ear is truly formed. The abbreviations (M3, P5, TT) are explained under the buttons, each tied to a tune you already know.
ear.mastery_hint: the uncertain ones return more often
ear.said_narrower: You said {guess} — {semitones} narrower than the answer.
ear.said_wider: You said {guess} — {semitones} wider than the answer.
rhythm.drill_hint: Build your sense of groove, downbeat and upbeat
rhythm.judging_help: How tight the timing window is around the click. Beginner forgives, Groover is the standard, Surgeon is metronome-strict.
rhythm.strict.tight_title: ±15ms (Tight) — the standard players are held to
rhythm.detection_help: How eagerly the app hears attacks from your instrument. Sensitive catches more; Strict ignores ringing tails.
rhythm.sens.sensitive_title: Catches quiet, closely spaced notes; may report a few extras
rhythm.sens.strict_title: Ignores ringing tails; may miss softly played notes
rhythm.warn_html:
Playing through a microphone? Use headphones — otherwise the mic hears the metronome and scores the click as a note you played. On a cable straight into your device this cannot happen.
One attack per note. Any pitch, any string. A strum reads as several notes; extras cost you nothing, but they cloud the picture.
rhythm.pick_for_tempo: Choose a study above to set its tempo.
rhythm.pick_a_drill: Choose a study to see what it trains.
rhythm.tempo_ceiling: Beyond {cap} BPM this subdivision runs too fast to be judged honestly.
rhythm.tempo_next_notch: One clean reading and the next step (+4 BPM) opens by itself.
rhythm.windows_note: Perfect ±{perfect} · Great ±{great} · Good ±{good} ms. Wider than that is a miss.
rhythm.sens_note.sensitive: Now catching notes it used to drop, at the cost of a few extras — which never lose you points.
rhythm.sens_note.balanced: Notes you played coming back as Missed? Move to Sensitive.
rhythm.sens_note.strict: Ignores ringing tails. If your own notes read as Missed, go the other way.
rhythm.gap_note: The click drops out for {bars} bars at a time.
rhythm.latency_measured: Measured. This delay comes off every attack, so the game judges the moment you actually played.
rhythm.latency_estimated: Estimated, not measured — every note will read late by whatever the real figure is. Twenty seconds fixes it.
results.title: Study concluded
results.at_ceiling: You are at this drill's ceiling ({bpm} BPM).
verdict.all_outside: Every note is there, none of them in the right window. Almost always that is the input delay being wrong, not your time: measure it again.
verdict.nothing_read: Nothing legible arrived. Check your input level and measure the input delay.
verdict.on_the_beat: You are in time, exactly where one must be.
verdict.rushing: You anticipate: about {ms} ms before the click. Haste is not energy.
verdict.dragging: You arrive after the click: about {ms} ms. Time is not chased, it is held.
verdict.spread_tight: And always by the same measure (±{ms} ms): that is the difficult part, and you hold it.
verdict.spread_wide: But each time differently: ±{ms} ms. A precision that comes and goes is not precision.
verdict.latency_hint: Every note landed {ms} ms {direction}, always by the same measure. That is not your time: it is the input delay. Try {suggested} ms instead of {current}.
extras.count_one: {count} sound did not match a note.
extras.count_other: {count} sounds did not match a note.
extras.tails: They arrive about {ms} ms after notes that did count{each}. That is the string still ringing and being heard twice — not something you played.
extras.scattered: They do not follow your notes, so it is the input rather than your playing: room noise, handling, or the metronome getting into the mic. The signal check tests exactly this.
extras.mixed: Some follow a note you played within {ms} ms, some do not.
extras.spammed: There were more stray sounds than the drill has notes, twice over, so this run does not count for a medal or a new tempo. If you were playing the drill and not strumming, something in your input is firing constantly — run the signal check.
advice.heading: What to study
advice.drift: You {direction} along the way: {ms} ms between the first bar and the last. Count aloud to the final note — when the counting stops, the time slips.
advice.weak_syllable: The weak point is the "{syllable}": you play it {ms} ms {direction} than everything else. Count aloud precisely there: nothing corrects itself.
advice.varies: There is no particular error: regularity is missing. Take off 8-10 BPM and stay there until the time is yours. Speed returns in an evening; discipline does not.
advice.steady_but_off: Regular, but always {ms} ms {direction} click. Make it disappear beneath your note: when you are upon it, you no longer hear it.
advice.steadiest_yet: The most regular reading you have given on this study: ±{ms} ms, against ±{previous}.
advice.level_with_best: You have repeated your best (±{ms} ms). To repeat oneself is already a quality.
input.healthy: Input clean — everything you played was counted
calib.title: Measure the delay
calib.check1_html: On a microphone? Headphones on. If the mic can hear the metronome, it scores the click as if you had played it. Plugged in by cable, you can skip this one.
calib.check2_html: First four clicks: listen, do not play. That is the mic check — nothing about you is being measured yet.
calib.check3_html: A 4-3-2-1 count-in brings you in, then one note on every click — same string, no strumming. Those notes measure two things at once: your delay, and how closely the game has to listen for your instrument.
calib.intro: Between the note you play and the note the program hears there is an instant, always the same. We measure it once and remove it: otherwise a player who is in time reads late, and on an error of that kind nothing can be studied.
calib.heard_something: Heard something. If that was you, wait for the count-in. If it was not, your mic is picking up the metronome.
calib.just_listen: Listen only: do not play. These clicks test the microphone, not you.
calib.mic_test_passed: Mic check clean — no metronome bleed.
calib.now_play: Now play: one note on every click. The same string throughout, no strumming. Better regular than accurate.
calib.get_ready: Attention: you come in on one. From there, one note per click, always the same string.
calib.nudged: Set by hand to {ms} ms. Play a drill and check: still reading behind? Add a little. Reading ahead? Take some off.
calib.bleed_failed:
The mic picked up {count} sounds during the listening step, so this run cannot be trusted.
If that was you playing: wait for the 4-3-2-1 next time.
If it was not: the metronome is leaking from your speakers into the mic. Headphones on, or the game scores its own click as a note you played.
calib.too_few_notes: Only {count} notes came through, even at the most sensitive setting — not enough to measure. Check your instrument is actually reaching the game, play a little harder, and give one note on every click.
calib.uneven_drift: steadily earlier or later as the run went on
calib.uneven_spread: anywhere within ±{ms} ms of the click
calib.uneven_msg: Your notes fell {how}: the delay cannot be established this way. One note per click, same string, no strumming. The steadiest reading wins.
calib.result_msg: From {taps} notes, within ±{spread} ms of one another. From now on that figure is removed from every attack: what is judged is when you played, not when the sound arrived.
calib.unusually_low: Unusually low for an input chain — if notes read early in the game, nudge it up.
calib.unusually_high: Unusually high — check you are not on a Bluetooth device, which adds a delay of its own.
calib.sens_set: Detection set to {label}: it heard {heard} of your {total} notes.
calib.sens_beat_next: The next setting down heard only {other}.
calib.sens_still_missed: If notes you played still come back Missed, that is the setting to move — it is on the setup screen.
error.mic_denied: Mic access denied. Grant permission and try again.
settings.intro_body: Learn every note on the guitar and bass neck. Choose a mission, play the note it calls for on the string it names — the mic confirms the hit in real time.
input.meter_title: Input level — it moves when the app hears you
input.monitor_title: Hear your instrument through the app
input.in_game: Meter paused — the game has the input
input.monitor_on: You are hearing yourself through the program
input.onboard_title: First of all: what the program should listen to
input.onboard_body: Your device's microphone if you play acoustically, your interface if the instrument is on a cable. Until this is right, nothing else can be: let us settle it now.
input.play_body: Watch the bar beside the picker: it must move. If it stays still, choose another device — the one your instrument is connected to.
input.heard_body: We are ready. The bar stays up there while you play, so you always know the program is listening.
input.denied_body: Microphone access was refused. Allow it from the padlock icon in the address bar, then try again — the app cannot hear a single note without it.
calib.gate_why: Twenty seconds, once. Until we know how long your sound takes to arrive, every note reads late — however well you keep time.
input.howl_hint: Hearing a whistle? That is the sound leaving your speakers and returning to the microphone: with headphones it does not happen.
rhythm.levels.4.tip: Keep counting through the rests. Silence is music: a rest is played in time too.
game.reading.title: The Page
game.reading.tag: Read the staff and play what is written
game.reading.desc: From the shape of a line to reading it at sight. First the picture, then the names, then you play what you read and the microphone confirms it. This is the study that needs the other three.
hint.reading: The first studies need no microphone. From the fourth on, you play what you read.
tip.reading: Reading tip: Learn three notes by sight and read every other one as a distance from them. Nobody counts up from the bottom line.
reading.panel_subtitle: From the shape of a line to reading it at sight
reading.pick_a_study: Choose a study to see what it trains.
reading.preview_caption.treble: Treble clef, and the three anchors named under it. Learn these by sight — everything else is a distance from them.
reading.preview_caption.bass: Bass clef, and the three anchors named under it. Learn these by sight — everything else is a distance from them.
reading.clef_help: The clef fixes which line is which note. Guitar reads in the treble clef, bass in the bass clef — and both sound an octave below what is written.
reading.clef.auto_title: The clef your instrument is written in
reading.clef.treble_title: The clef guitar music is written in
reading.clef.bass_title: The clef bass music is written in
reading.clef_note.treble: Treble clef. It curls around the note on the second line — that is where its name comes from, and it is your first anchor.
reading.clef_note.bass: Bass clef. Its two dots straddle the fourth line — that is where its name comes from, and it is your first anchor.
reading.sound_desc: The note is played the moment it is answered. A sign tied to a sound is learned; a sign on its own is memorised, and memory fades.
reading.neck_desc: After a missed note, where it lies under the hand. Turn it off once the hand goes there without being told.
reading.kind.name: naming
reading.ask.contour_updown: Is the second note higher or lower?
reading.ask.name: Which note is this?
reading.ask.sight: Read straight through at {bpm} BPM. Do not stop.
reading.wrong_contour: No. It was {answer}. Read the shape, not the names.
reading.wrong_octave: The letter is right, the octave is not: what is written is {note}{octave}. Read the place, not only the name.
reading.nothing_played: Nothing arrived. That was {note} — keep going anyway: the line does not wait.
reading.hint.contour: The dashed rule runs through the first note. Now look at the second one.
ear.root_note: The reference is {note}. Every answer is a distance from it — change it and the same interval sounds from a new place.
rhythm.printed_caption: The first two bars, as they would be printed.
